reconcile.connective: Matthew Henry folds both Gospels into one timeline: the family stayed in Bethlehem nearly two years, so the magi's house doesn't erase their Nazareth home.

discrepancy.connective: Strauss objected that the accounts are incompatible since Matthew never mentions a prior Nazareth residence or what brought the family to Bethlehem.

skeptic.name: David Friedrich Strauss
skeptic.work: The Life of Jesus Critically Examined
skeptic.attribution: David Friedrich Strauss, The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1835/1846)

excerpts.excerpt_text: …for aught that appears, he continued nearly two years after at Bethlehem, and no further notice was taken of him till these wise men came.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explains why the magi find the family already settled 'in a house' (Matt 2:11) rather than at the birth-manger: Henry has them remaining in Bethlehem for up to two years, the standard combined-timeline move that lets Matthew's silence about a prior Nazareth home coexist with Luke's Nazareth-to-Bethlehem itinerary.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact discrepancy under 'Christ's infancy — order of events' (Matt. ii. 1-23 vs. Luke ii. 4-39), naming Strauss's objection that Matthew omits the residence at Nazareth before the nativity, and answering that the silence of one evangelist proves little, proposing the harmonizing order: journey from Nazareth to Bethlehem, birth, temple presentation, the magi (received in a 'house'), flight to Egypt, and settlement at Nazareth.

link.title: Do the narratives of Jesus' birth contradict each other?
link.note: live apologetic treatment arguing Joseph and Mary remained in Bethlehem after the birth, staying in the 'house' of Matthew 2:11, before eventually returning to Nazareth
